title: Sonauli Border Crossing Guide for Indians and Foreigners
meta_description: Sonauli–Belahiya border guide: documents for Indians, Nepal visa on arrival for foreigners, Indian e-Visa limits, vehicle customs pass, currency, timings and scams.
summary: Sonauli (India) and Belahiya (Nepal) form the main tourist crossing between the two countries, 26 km from Lumbini. Indians walk across with a passport or voter ID and need no visa. Other nationals get Indian exit and Nepal entry stamps, with visas on arrival at Belahiya. Indian vehicles need a per-day customs pass. Check current status before you travel.

sections.heading: Where the crossing is and how it works
paras: The border runs between Sonauli, a small town in Uttar Pradesh's Maharajganj district, and Belahiya, which merges into Bhairahawa (Siddharthanagar) in Nepal, about 4 km to the north. A gateway arch marks the line on the main road. Both sides are busy with shops, rickshaws, buses and goods trucks from early morning until late at night. India has built an Integrated Check Post at Sonauli to handle immigration, customs and cargo.

For Indian and Nepali citizens, the border is open and there is no immigration stamp; you simply walk or drive across, though security forces on both sides may check identity documents and luggage. For all other nationalities, the crossing is a formal international border with separate Indian and Nepali immigration offices, a few hundred metres apart. Foreigners must stop at both and must not cross without stamps.

sections.heading: Documents for Indian citizens
paras: Indian citizens do not need a visa for Nepal. Under the rules published by the Embassy of India in Kathmandu, adults need either a valid Indian passport or an Election Commission of India voter ID card. Children under 15 and adults over 65 can usually travel on another photo ID with proof of age, such as Aadhaar, a PAN card, a driving licence or a ration card, and students aged 15 to 18 may use an identity certificate from their school principal. For adults aged 15 to 65, Aadhaar alone is generally not accepted.

When a family travels together, each person should carry their own valid document; do not rely on one adult's ID for the group. Keep the document handy for the return crossing and for domestic flights in Nepal, where Indian nationals need it to pay the rupee fare. These rules have been revised in the past, so check current status before you travel.

sections.heading: Documents and visas for foreign nationals
paras: Third-country nationals need a passport valid for at least six months and, if entering Nepal, a Nepal visa. Most nationalities can get a tourist visa on arrival at the Belahiya immigration office. Fees are paid in US dollars cash: as we understand current rates, about US$ 30 for 15 days, US$ 50 for 30 days and US$ 125 for 90 days, all multiple entry. You need a passport photo, and filling in the online arrival form on Nepal's immigration website within 15 days before arrival saves time. A few nationalities must obtain a visa in advance.

Leaving India, foreigners must get an exit stamp at the Indian immigration office in Sonauli. Re-entering India by land at Sonauli is more complicated: under current rules, the Indian e-Visa is accepted only at designated airports, seaports and a small number of land crossings, and Sonauli has not been one of them. If you plan to return to India by road, hold a regular paper visa, or route your trip so you fly out of Nepal. Check current status before you travel.

sections.heading: Crossing step by step
paras: Coming from Gorakhpur, buses and taxis drop you in Sonauli a few hundred metres before the arch. Foreigners go first to the Indian immigration office on the main road for an exit stamp. Then walk through the arch into Nepal and look for the Nepal immigration office at Belahiya, a short walk beyond the arch, where you complete the arrival form, pay the visa fee and get your entry stamp. Indians simply walk through, showing ID if asked.

On the Nepal side, taxis, jeeps and cycle rickshaws wait to take you to Bhairahawa bus park, 4 km away, or directly to Lumbini, 26 km away. Fix the fare before you set off; our packages include a private car from the border. The whole process takes 15–30 minutes for Indians and roughly one to two hours for other nationals, depending on queues.

sections.heading: Bringing an Indian vehicle
paras: Indian private vehicles can enter Nepal through Belahiya. For day visits to the nearby market, a free registration pass is issued at the checkpoint. For longer trips, the driver must obtain a customs pass, often called a bhansar permit, from the Bhairahawa customs office, paying a per-day charge that is higher for cars and jeeps than for motorcycles. A vehicle may stay in Nepal for a maximum of 30 days in a calendar year.

Carry the registration certificate, a valid driving licence, insurance, pollution certificate and the owner's ID; if the owner is not travelling, carry an authorisation letter. Nepal drives on the left like India, but hill roads are narrow and steep, and some routes have restrictions on heavy vehicles. Charges and paperwork are revised from time to time, so check current status before you travel.

sections.heading: Money, SIM cards and timings
paras: The Nepali rupee is pegged at about NPR 1.6 to INR 1, and Indian rupees are accepted widely near the border and in tourist areas. Since late 2025, Nepal has allowed Indian ₹200 and ₹500 notes issued after November 2016 to be carried up to ₹25,000 per person. Banks and ATMs in Bhairahawa give better rates for other currencies than border money changers. Nepal Telecom and Ncell SIM cards are sold in Bhairahawa with an ID and a photo.

Indians can technically cross at any hour, but immigration offices for foreigners keep daytime and evening hours, and the onward roads are safer in daylight. We advise crossing between 8 am and 4 pm, and avoiding Sundays and major festivals when shoppers create long queues.

sections.heading: Common problems and how to avoid them
paras: Ignore touts who offer to arrange visas, stamps or vehicle passes for a fee; the official counters are straightforward, and paying middlemen risks fake receipts. Foreign travellers who walk across without an Indian exit stamp or Nepal entry stamp face fines and trouble when leaving later. Bus tickets sold in Gorakhpur or Varanasi as through tickets to Kathmandu or Pokhara often involve changing buses at the border, so check what is included.

Finally, keep copies of your passport, visa and ID in your phone and on paper, and carry a few passport photos. If you are travelling with our team, our representative meets you at a fixed point and walks you through each step.

faqs.q: Is Sonauli border open for tourists?
faqs.a: Yes. Sonauli–Belahiya is the busiest tourist crossing between India and Nepal, open to Indian and Nepali citizens at all hours and to other nationals during immigration office hours. Foreigners get Indian exit and Nepal entry stamps here, with visas on arrival available at Belahiya. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: What ID do Indians need at Sonauli?
faqs.a: A valid Indian passport or voter ID card for adults. Children under 15 and adults over 65 can usually use another photo ID with age proof, such as Aadhaar or PAN, and students aged 15–18 a school identity certificate. Aadhaar alone is generally not accepted for adults aged 15 to 65.

faqs.q: Can I get a Nepal visa on arrival at Sonauli?
faqs.a: Yes, at the Nepal immigration office at Belahiya, just across the line from Sonauli. Most nationalities can get 15, 30 or 90-day tourist visas, paid in US dollars cash. Bring a passport photo and fill in the online arrival form in advance to save time. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Can foreigners enter India at Sonauli on an e-Visa?
faqs.a: Under current rules, no. The Indian e-Visa is valid for entry only at listed airports, seaports and a few land crossings, and Sonauli has not been included. E-Visa holders can generally exit India here. To re-enter India by road at Sonauli, hold a regular visa. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Can I take my Indian car to Nepal through Sonauli?
faqs.a: Yes. Get a customs pass at the Bhairahawa customs office, paying a per-day charge, with the RC, driving licence, insurance and pollution certificate. Vehicles may stay up to 30 days in a calendar year. Same-day market visits only need a free registration pass. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: How long does it take to cross the Sonauli border?
faqs.a: Indian citizens on foot usually take 15–30 minutes. Foreign nationals should allow one to two hours for Indian exit and Nepal visa formalities. Vehicles needing a customs pass can take one to two hours more, especially on weekends and festival days.

faqs.q: What are the Sonauli border timings?
faqs.a: The crossing is open around the clock for Indian and Nepali citizens. Immigration offices serving other nationals keep daytime and evening hours. We recommend crossing between 8 am and 4 pm for shorter queues and daylight onward travel. Hours can change, so check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Can I use Indian rupees after crossing into Nepal?
faqs.a: Yes. Indian rupees are accepted widely in Bhairahawa, Lumbini and most tourist areas at about NPR 1.6 per INR. Since late 2025, ₹200 and ₹500 notes issued after November 2016 are allowed up to ₹25,000 per person. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: How far is Lumbini from the Sonauli border?
faqs.a: About 26 km, 45 minutes to an hour by car. Taxis and shared jeeps wait on the Nepal side at Belahiya, and local buses run from Bhairahawa bus park. Pokhara is about 190 km and Kathmandu about 280 km from the border.
